# Signed complete global cuts and isolated free-facet realization

This note extends physical SPEED addition to continuous convex fields of
arbitrary sign. Unlike the inward construction, it must not intersect with
the original body or add zero cuts that block outward motion. It proves a
precise compatibility condition realizing the signed facet motions used in
`candidate a7b11eee1eaaf72e`.

It adds regular-cap and continuous weighted responses. Positive-area
supporting-cap responses remain nonlinear and require the separately proved
directional inverse theorem. No OC payment is claimed.

## 1. Complete baseline arrays and signed fields

Let P be finite and lattice-complete, and let positive compact convex K_z
satisfy every anchored Minkowski inclusion. Write B=conv P and h_z(u)
for unit continuous normal u. For each of finitely many actions a, take a
finite index set I_a, continuous support planes ell_ai(u,z), affine in z,
and continuous fields V_ai(u,z,X), convex in the full physical variables
(z,X). Fields are finite everywhere and may have either sign. Assume

    ell_ai(u,z)>=h_z(u),
    min_(i in I_a) ell_ai(u,z)=h_z(u)                  (1)

for EVERY sampled z and EVERY unit u, for EACH action. The second condition
is called completeness here; it is an explicit hypothesis.

Define the actual ambient body without intersection with the original hull:

    C_a(t)={ (z,X):z in B,
       u.X+t V_ai(u,z,X)<=ell_ai(u,z)
                  for all i in I_a and all unit u }.              (2)

At t=0 its integer fibers are exactly K_z by (1). Between sampled bases
C_a(0) can be larger than their canonical hull; this is harmless for the
mixed data. For t>0 use the canonical hull of its sampled fibers if a
canonical representative is required. It has the SAME sampled fibers,
because C_a(t) is convex. No unchanged real-base-fiber claim is made.

A simple source of complete arrays is the finite family of support planes
indexed by every p in P, each touching h_p(u), using the archived bounded
continuous feasible support slopes. If all planes of one action have the
same signed convex field, their integer fibers agree exactly with the
corresponding signed canonical normal-roof deformation.

## 2. Uniform boundedness, positivity, and signed radial control

For small t>=0, (2) is a compact convex set with positive sampled fibers and
projection B. We give the details because outward motion is now allowed.

Fix a compact neighborhood of B times a continuous ball. Joint continuity
bounds all fields there. Convexity gives a UNIFORM lower linear bound in X
for z in B:

    V_ai(u,z,X)>=-C(1+|X|).                           (3)

For example bound V at (z,0) and on (z,X) with |X|<=1; restricting the
convex function to the ray through X and using its value at radius one
proves (3). The finite indices and compact normal/base sets give one C.
The baselines are uniformly bounded on B. Choosing u=X/|X| in a defining
inequality gives

    |X|-t C(1+|X|)<=sup ell.

For t C<1/2 this supplies a common bounding ball for ALL of (2). Hence the
fields are uniformly bounded in absolute value, say by A, on this ball.

At an integer fiber, completeness and its defining inequalities give

    u.X<=h_z(u)+t A  for all u,
    C_a(t)_z subset K_z+t A Ball.                    (4)

If o_z+r_z Ball subset K_z, then

    o_z+(1-t A/r_z)(K_z-o_z) subset C_a(t)_z          (5)

for small t. Its support slack is at least tA against every baseline,
while its added field is at most A. Thus every sampled fiber remains
positive, has Hausdorff distance O(t) from K_z, and has radial displacement
O(t) from an old interior origin. Every vertex of B is sampled, so convexity
and (5) give projection exactly B. Convexity also proves all new anchored
inclusions without an independent compatibility approximation.

The optional rational perpendicular thickening for deficient base rank is
as in the inward source: a fixed ball below the shortest nonzero projected
lattice vector restores ambient interior and introduces no new integer
fibers. It is not claimed to stay inside any originally supplied ambient
body.

## 3. Exact signed speed formula

At a regular old boundary point X of K_z, let u be its unique outward unit
normal. By completeness the active index set

    I_a(z,u)={i:ell_ai(u,z)=h_z(u)}

is nonempty. Then the actual signed inward normal speed is

    v_az(X)=max_(i in I_a(z,u)) V_ai(u,z,X).           (6)

There is NO maximum with zero. In particular (6) can be negative.

For a direct proof write the new endpoint on the ray from o_z as
X_s=o_z+(1-s)(X-o_z), with signed s=O(t). For an old active cut,

    s u.(X-o_z)>=t V_ai(u,z,X_s),

which gives the lower bound on s/t. At a new radial endpoint some defining
cut is active, since the compact continuous family of constraints would
otherwise permit radial extension. Along a subsequence its index is fixed
and its normal converges. The old slack

    ell_ai(u,z)-u.X=[ell_ai(u,z)-h_z(u)]+[h_z(u)-u.X]

is nonnegative and O(t). Its limiting normal therefore supports X and
its limiting index is old-active. The active equality and nonnegative old
slack give the matching upper bound on s/t. The radial denominator tends
to the positive u.(X-o_z). This proves (6), for either sign of s.

The radial Jacobian gives bounded a.e. signed first speeds and all the
uniform weighted-shell expansions already proved for signed radial paths.
In d=1 this is the two-endpoint calculation with counting measure.

## 4. Product-plane construction adds the signed speeds

For nonnegative desired coefficients t_a, choose positive baseline weights
rho_a summing to one, independently of t_a. For every index tuple put

    ell_tuple=sum_a rho_a ell_(a i_a),
    V_tuple=sum_a t_a V_(a i_a).                      (7)

The baseline is affine, the field convex and continuous, and completeness
is preserved. Each sampled slack is a positive weighted sum of nonnegative
component slacks. A tuple is active exactly when ALL component indices
are active. Their nonempty active sets are independent. Formula (6) gives

    v_new(z,X)=sum_a t_a v_a(z,X)                     (8)

surface-almost everywhere. This is one actual compatible path of form (2).
It is not Minkowski interpolation of the separately deformed fibers.

Zero desired coefficients are permitted; baseline weights must stay
positive. There is no topological-closure or varying-number-of-actions
assertion. Most importantly, inserting zero-field planes or intersecting
with the old canonical hull would replace negative speeds by zero and
invalidate this signed conclusion.

Continuous boundary-weight responses add by (8), including total volume,
energy envelopes, and covariance moments. Proper or strict full/empty
fixed caps also have linear first losses, so regular buffered responses
in the companion note add exactly. This proves an actual convex response
cone in that specified signed complete-cut class.

At supporting caps this final statement MUST be qualified. For the endpoint
of [-1,1] and the fixed cap X>=1, inward endpoint speed 1 has loss zero,
speed -1 has loss -1, and their sum speed zero has loss zero. Therefore
supporting losses do not add even though speeds do. Use
`candidate 8d34ae3d0117f855`
for these nonlinear responses, with the new SUMMED actual speed.

## 5. A sufficient actual isolation condition for one free facet

The directed forced-contact relation is defined in
`candidate 4bf40258fc44a4e6`.
For a source q, the target p is forced at u iff a tight anchored support
representation of q uses p with positive weight. The archived theorem
supplies ONE bounded continuous support slope for every source q whose
contact set is exactly its forced set, simultaneously for all normals.

Suppose K_p is a polytope with a facet F of unit outward normal u0, and at
u0 the base p is isolated in BOTH directions of this relation:

    no z!=p is forced for source p;
    p is not forced for any source q!=p.             (9)

These are conditions on ACTUAL support equalities. By finite base count
and continuity of the forced-only selected slacks, there is a normal
neighborhood U of u0 in which the source-p plane has strict slack at every
other sampled base, and every other source plane has strict slack at p.
Use the complete baseline array consisting of all these selected planes.
At p, its only active plane in U is the source-p plane. At every other
base that plane is inactive, while its own zero-field plane is active.

Choose a continuous normal cutoff chi>=0 with chi(u0)=1 and support in U,
so small that it contains no other facet normal of K_p. Given ANY globally
finite convex continuous function phi(X), assign

    V_p(u,z,X)=chi(u) phi(X),
    V_q=0 for q!=p.                                 (10)

The fields are convex in (z,X), may have either sign, and satisfy the
signed theorem. Its ONLY nonzero measured boundary speed is phi on F:
all other sampled fibers have speed zero; the other facets of K_p have
speed zero; nonfacet polytope joins have zero surface measure.

For phi=1 and phi=-1 these are the two parallel facet motions needed by
the companion Jensen test. For the outward tent, identify the affine hull
of F with R^(d-1), let p_F be its centroid, and write

    F={x:ell_r(x)<=1, all r},  ell_r(p_F)=0.

Then T(x)=1-max_r ell_r(x) is the pyramid tent on F, and
phi=max_r ell_r-1=-T is globally convex on that affine space. Extend it
constantly in the facet-normal coordinate to a finite convex function on
R^d. Formula (10) realizes the exact outward-tent first speed.

All these actions use the SAME complete baselines, and nonnegative sums
of their convex signed fields remain convex. Thus their whole finite
response cone, including both parallel signs and the outward tent, is
physically realized. This closes the cone-feasibility premise of the
companion free-facet argument under the explicit isolation condition (9).
No outward apex is assumed to affect only one patch in the absence of (9).

## 6. Scope and relation to the old potential cone

Condition (9) is a sufficient compatibility hypothesis, not a claim that
a bad minimizing family has an isolated facet. A shared contact may force
cost on several sampled patches, and the construction retains that cost
unless isolation has actually been proved.

The signed theorem is an exact finite realization result. It does not by
itself add strict separating power beyond the archived signed-affine plus
convex-potential class. On a fixed common compact neighborhood, choose A
so that V+A>0. Then V=max(V+A,0)-A there: one nonnegative globally convex
field minus a constant realizes the same boundary trace. The earlier
penalty approximation handles contact maxima, with its stated order of
limits. No new numerical payment is inferred merely by renaming that cone.

What is newly supplied for the companion application is precise: the
three free-facet tests and their finite nonnegative combinations have one
actual compatible cut realization under (9). The accompanying covariance
Hessian obstruction is therefore a valid physical first-order exclusion
in this bounded geometric scope.
